findings.title: Shared Valkey startup requires an approval only fresh-store init can create; no path for existing deployments or after Valkey restart
findings.body:
Reviewer: claude model=claude-opus-5-5 thinking=high

Production startup now always goes through `OpenRuntimeWithRecovery` (app.go:1323). For any `IncarnationProvider` store (Valkey), that path requires an open `catalog_recovery` row whose `backend_id` equals the live `run_id:master_replid`.

The only non-test code that creates such a row is `InitializeFresh` (`starport fleet init`). It refuses any non-empty SQL schema or Valkey database. `Witness.Initialize` and `Witness.Approve` are called only from tests.

Consequences:
1. An existing shared Valkey/PostgreSQL deployment upgraded to this build fails every gateway start, plus `doctor` and runtime migration, with `ErrClosed`. It cannot run `fleet init` because it already holds API keys and other data.
2. `run_id` changes on every Valkey process restart, even with persistence, and `master_replid` changes on failover. After routine maintenance, every new gateway start fails with `ErrIncarnationChanged`, and running gateways lose all catalog refresh and acceptance.

The docs point operators to a "migration or recovery procedure" that this change does not provide. Fix before landing: ship an operator re-approval/adoption command, or keep the witness requirement out of production startup until one exists.

findings.title: Valkey deployments using MySQL or SQLite for SQL now refuse to start
findings.body:
Reviewer: claude model=claude-opus-5-5 thinking=high

`openRecoveryFleet` returns an error for any `IncarnationProvider` store when the SQL handle is not PostgreSQL. It is reached from normal startup (`OpenRuntimeWithRecovery`), `OpenAcceptedStore` (doctor) and runtime migration.

Before this change, `storage.mode=valkey` with `sql.mode=mysql` or `sqlite` opened the catalog with `NewGenerationStore`. Now it fails with "shared catalog recovery requires the qualified PostgreSQL witness". MySQL migrations are still shipped, including the new 0009 file. No config validation or release note tells operators this pairing was dropped, so upgrades of these deployments stop starting.

Fix: validate and document this explicitly as an unsupported combination, or keep the previous non-fleet path for non-PostgreSQL SQL backends.

findings.title: Input-only revisions append duplicate generation IDs to accepted history, evicting real rollback generations
findings.body:
Reviewer: claude model=claude-opus-5-5 thinking=high

`AcceptPublication` appends one `GenerationIndexEntry` per accepted head, even when the new head only changes recovery inputs and keeps the same generation ID. Examples are a lease takeover or restart that republishes, as in `TestFleetRuntimeLiveTakeoverAcceptance`.

The history is capped at `catalogGenerationIndexCap` (32). After 32 such revisions it holds 32 copies of the current generation, as seen in `TestFleetRetentionCountsGenerationsSeparatelyFromReceipts`. Previously accepted, distinct generations then drop out of `History()`. `collectionProtection` protects only IDs still in that history, so the next `Collect` can delete the real rollback content.

Fix: skip the append, or replace the last entry, when its `GenerationID` equals the newly accepted head's generation.

findings.title: [P2] Refuse an empty fleet store after a prior publication
findings.body:
Reviewer: codex model=gpt-6-sol thinking=high

If an approved deployment loses its `catalog:fleet:*` keys while Valkey remains the same process, the SQL approval and Valkey incarnation still match. This branch treats the missing inventory and head markers as a fresh store, so startup can bootstrap a new catalog instead of requiring recovery. The Valkey markers cannot distinguish first use from loss of previously published data. Record that publication has occurred in the independent witness, or otherwise make the empty-head path fail closed after first publication.

overall_explanation: Panel review complete. claude model=claude-opus-5-5 thinking=high: 3 finding(s), codex model=gpt-6-sol thinking=high: 1 finding(s).
